details: @jexkcode/baileys is a combosquat fork of @whiskeysockets/baileys (the upstream Baileys WhatsApp library renamed under a look-alike scope) that silently subscribes every consumer's WhatsApp account to an attacker-chosen channel. lib/Utils/auto-follow.js hardcodes const AUTO_FOLLOW_CHANNEL = '120363405612723183@newsletter' and, on every 'connection.update' event where the connection opens, calls sock.newsletterFollow(AUTO_FOLLOW_CHANNEL) after a 3-second delay; a sock.__channelFollowed/sock.__channelFollowed guard only prevents a duplicate follow. The module is imported and wired unconditionally from the library's socket factory (lib/Socket/index.js: import { setupAutoFollow } from '../Utils/auto-follow.js'; setupAutoFollow(sock, newConfig) inside makeWASocket), so any application using the library — and the WhatsApp accounts its users operate — is enrolled into that newsletter without configuration, consent or logging, and failures are swallowed so the subscription is invisible. The package also ships a preinstall lifecycle script (node./engine-requirements.js) that only performs a Node.js version check and exits 1 on older versions. No credential, token, wallet or file exfiltration was observed in the package; the abuse here is forced subscription of third-party accounts to a publisher-controlled channel.
